sentence: This project builds molecules that block DNA-mutating enzymes active in cancer cells and help study how the enzymes work.
This project studies how an immune signal controls an RNA binding protein in regulatory T cells during colorectal cancer development.
This project builds a nanopore and computer method to find and measure a chemical change called pseudouridine in mRNA.
This project studies how the immune system becomes activated to cause autoimmune responses and explores a way to target this role.
This project uses machine learning that protects privacy to find subtypes of asthma in children and how they change over time.
This project tries to turn stem cells into mural cells, a type of cell in blood vessels, and studies them in a miniature organ model.
This project studies how DNA replication starts in multicellular organisms, using a single-molecule approach to see how a helicase is loaded onto origins.
This project studies how reactive astrocytes contribute to Alzheimer's disease by isolating these rare cells from archived brain samples.
This project studies how methamphetamine acts on a trace-amine associated receptor to cause aversion and reduce its intake.
This project studies how cancer and the drug cisplatin injure the kidney and tests treatments that block this injury and chronic kidney disease.
This project builds transgenic rats in which genes can be changed in particular tissues or at particular times.
This project tests whether a bat protein that binds RNA blocks viruses by attaching to a sequence in viral RNA.
This project builds experimental and computational tools to study how drugs interact and cause adverse reactions.
This project uses mouse models to find out how a gene affects brain growth and patterning during development in autism spectrum disorder.
This project studies a mouse missing a gene linked to autism and neurodevelopmental disorders to see what changes in the brain and behavior.
This project tries to find out what leads to better outcomes in people with rare cystic fibrosis mutations.
This project tests how developmental alcohol exposure affects the organization and function of auditory areas of the cortex.
This project studies how a virus disrupts the placenta and builds organoid models to look for ways to target these effects.
This project builds a platform that can sequence very large numbers of single cells from blood and tissue samples.
This project studies how daily stress and coping change during a weight loss program and how they relate to weight lost.
